title: The job interview

fn.en: Answer the questions a job interview really asks, and write a CV that gets you into the room.

lines: I’ve got a university [degree|diploma|award] in journalism. 🎓
I’ve worked as a sports journalist [for|since|from] six years. 💼
I’m [currently|current|currency] working for an ice hockey magazine. ⏱
I’d really like to get [into|in|on] online publishing. ➡️

sub.en: Look at the answers. Which grammar does each interview question pull out of you?

items.q: “How much experience do you have?” — “I’ve worked as a journalist ___ six years.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 34: duration is the single most common answer in an interview.

items.q: “What are you doing now?” — “I’m ___ working for a magazine.”
“Why do you want this job?” — “I’d like ___ into online publishing.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 35: the infinitive after would like.

items.q: “What are your strengths?” — “I’m good at ___ people.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 28: after a preposition, the -ing form.

items.q: “And your weakness?” — “I find it hard ___ no.”
“Have you ever managed a team?” — “Yes, ___.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 17: a short answer never uses the contraction.

items.q: “What would you do if a deadline moved?” — “I ___ tell the client first.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 31: the second conditional for a hypothetical question.

items.q: “Tell me about the award.” — “I ___ it in 2019.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 17 again: a finished year takes the Past Simple.

use: How much experience do you have?
tts: So, on with the interview. First of all, tell me, Danielle, what qualifications have you got for this job? — Well, I’ve got a university degree in journalism, and that included not just newspaper and magazine journalism but also radio, TV and, of course, online journalism.
OK, good, and how much experience do you have? In sports journalism, I mean. — I’ve worked as a sports journalist for six years. My first job was working for a local newspaper.
And what are you doing at the moment? — I’m currently working for an ice hockey magazine. But I’d really like to get into online publishing.

acts.title: Danielle Marchand — sports journalist
text: PERSONAL PROFILE — Sports journalist with six years’ experience in print and magazine work, currently at an ice hockey monthly. Looking to move into online publishing. Fast, accurate, and comfortable interviewing people who do not want to be interviewed.
2021–present · Staff writer, Rink Monthly. Two features a month plus match reports. Set up the magazine’s live match blog, which now has 40,000 monthly readers.
2018–2021 · Sports reporter, Le Quotidien de l’Est. Local football and hockey. Won the Young Sports Journalist award, 2019.
EDUCATION — 2014–2018 · BA Journalism, Université de Montréal. Newspaper, magazine, radio, TV and online.
SKILLS — French and English (both native). Basic Spanish. Video editing. Live blogging.

write.q: CAPSTONE · Write your own CV: the six sections of the model. Then add the four interview answers underneath — how much experience you have, what you are doing now, why you want the job, and one strength and one weakness. Use for or since, one infinitive with to, and one -ing form after a preposition.
write.model: MARAT ZHAKSYBEK · Almaty · m.zhaksybek@email.kz · +7 701 555 0143 — PERSONAL PROFILE: Data analyst with four years’ experience in retail reporting, currently at Kaspi Retail. Looking to move into a role with more client contact. Fast with numbers and unusually willing to explain them twice. — WORK EXPERIENCE: 2021–present · Data assistant, Kaspi Retail. Weekly figures for four regions. Built the reporting template the team now uses. 2019–2021 · Junior analyst, Halyk Bank. — EDUCATION: 2015–2019 · BA Economics, KIMEP. — SKILLS: Kazakh, Russian, English. SQL, Excel, Power BI. — REFERENCES: Available on request. — INTERVIEW ANSWERS: I’ve worked in data for four years. I’m currently at Kaspi Retail. I’d like to get into a role where I explain the numbers, not just produce them. I’m good at building things other people can use. I find it hard to say no to extra work.

speak.q: CAPSTONE · Answer these five interview questions out loud, in full sentences: Tell me about yourself. How much experience do you have? What are you doing at the moment? Why do you want this job? What is your greatest weakness — and what are you doing about it?
speak.model: I’m a data analyst and I’ve worked in retail reporting for four years. I’m currently at Kaspi Retail, where I prepare the weekly figures for four regions. I’d like to get into a role with more client contact, because explaining the numbers is the part I do best and do least. My weakness is that I find it hard to say no to extra work — I’ve started blocking two hours a day and it is slowly working.
